topics.label: Introduction and lecture framing
topics.groupedBecause: The opening frames the lecture as an integration of previously introduced immune cells and molecules.

topics.label: Principles of innate recognition of infection and damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how innate immunity identifies danger through molecular patterns and receptors suited to detecting them.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor families and inflammatory signalling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how specific pattern recognition systems translate danger detection into inflammatory responses.

topics.label: Sentinel cell activation and leukocyte recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how activated sentinel cells generate signals that mobilise an inflammatory response at the infection site.

topics.label: Lymphatic transport and adaptive immune priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how drainage from infected tissues enables dendritic cells to initiate adaptive immune responses in lymph nodes.

topics.label: Excessive systemic inflammation and septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how excessive inflammatory activation becomes a life-threatening systemic response.

topics.label: Passive and active resolution of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inflammatory activity subsides through the withdrawal of stimulation and the action of inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Tissue repair and persistent inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the outcomes of incomplete recovery from tissue inflammation, including chronic damage and containment of persistent infection.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture on complement
topics.groupedBecause: The closing ends the lecture and identifies complement as the subject of the next session.
